static-spa.recommended_path: Azure Static Web Apps. Free tier covers most static use cases. Drop your build output (dist/, out/, build/). Custom domain + free managed certs included.
caveats: Free tier has a 250 MB app size limit and ~100 MB per artifact.
API (Functions) on Static Web Apps Free is also size-limited; Standard plan removes the limit.

nextjs.recommended_path: Azure Static Web Apps (App Router static export) or Azure App Service / Container Apps for full SSR. SWA Hybrid Next.js (preview) supports App Router + RSC; for production-grade SSR + ISR pick App Service Linux (Node 20) or Container Apps. Functions also works for API-only routes.
caveats: ISR / on-demand revalidation requires App Service or Container Apps — Static Web Apps does not run a Next.js server.
next/image with sharp needs a Linux App Service plan or Container Apps; sharp is fine on Linux but flaky on Windows plans.
Server Actions = POST endpoints: rate-limit via Front Door / App Gateway WAF.
AAD authentication via App Service Easy Auth removes most NextAuth boilerplate.

astro.recommended_path: Azure Static Web Apps with the @astrojs/cloudflare or @astrojs/node adapter (use node adapter for SSR on App Service). Static-only Astro sites are an exact fit for Static Web Apps.
caveats: SSR on Static Web Apps is via the integrated Functions runtime — not full Node.
If you need Astro endpoints with arbitrary Node modules, deploy to App Service or Container Apps.

sveltekit.recommended_path: Azure Static Web Apps with the SvelteKit adapter, or App Service Linux for full Node SSR.
caveats: Form actions are POST-heavy — verify rate-limit rules on Front Door / App Gateway.

remix.recommended_path: Azure Static Web Apps for static + minimal-server-side, or App Service / Container Apps for full Remix SSR with arbitrary Node.
caveats: Loaders/actions run on the server — verify your runtime is Node 20 on App Service Linux.

nuxt.recommended_path: Azure Static Web Apps via Nitro azure preset, or App Service Linux for full SSR.
caveats: Nuxt's Nitro engine handles abstraction; verify your Nitro modules are Node-compatible.

vite-spa.recommended_path: Azure Static Web Apps. Pure static — drop the dist/ output.

express.recommended_path: Azure App Service Linux (Node 20) or Azure Container Apps. Both run Express directly — no rewrite. Container Apps gives you scale-to-zero + Dapr if you want it; App Service is simpler.
caveats: App Service basic-auth (SCM/FTP) should be DISABLED — use deployment slots + GitHub Actions OIDC.
Sessions in memory don't survive scale events — move to Azure Cache for Redis.

fastify.recommended_path: Same as Express. App Service or Container Apps run Fastify directly.
caveats: fastify-multipart streaming uploads → Blob Storage SDK from Functions or Container Apps.

nestjs.recommended_path: Azure App Service Linux or Container Apps. NestJS runs unmodified.
caveats: NestJS microservices via TCP/Redis transport: prefer Container Apps for the inter-service networking.

hono.recommended_path: Azure Functions (Node) or Azure Container Apps. Hono's Node adapter is mature; for low-latency edge use Front Door in front.

wordpress.recommended_path: Azure App Service has an official WordPress on Linux managed offering (PHP 8.x + MariaDB Flexible Server). Fits if you want managed PHP. Otherwise, Azure VM + Bitnami AMI / docker-compose, behind Front Door + WAF.
caveats: App Service WordPress offering uses MySQL Flexible Server — check pricing tier carefully (Burstable vs General Purpose).
wp-admin / xmlrpc.php / wp-cron.php should be IP-allowlisted via App Service IP restrictions or Front Door custom rules.
Real cron via App Service WebJob, not wp-cron.

laravel.recommended_path: Azure App Service Linux (PHP 8.2+) runs Laravel directly — composer install + artisan migrate. Container Apps is the alternative for Docker-native deployments.
caveats: Queue workers stay on App Service WebJobs or Container Apps as a separate service.
Sessions: redis driver pointed at Azure Cache for Redis.
Storage: Laravel filesystem driver 'azure' (league/flysystem-azure-blob-storage).

rails.recommended_path: Azure App Service Linux (Ruby) or Container Apps. App Service has Ruby support; Container Apps is simpler for Docker-based deployments.
caveats: ActionCable WebSockets work on App Service (enable Web Sockets) and Container Apps.
Sidekiq workers: separate App Service Web App for the worker process or a Container App with scale-to-zero.

django.recommended_path: Azure App Service Linux (Python 3.11+) or Container Apps. Both run Django directly.
caveats: Channels (WebSockets) work on App Service with Daphne/Uvicorn.
Celery workers: separate App Service or Container App; broker = Azure Service Bus or Redis Cache.

fastapi.recommended_path: App Service Linux Python with Gunicorn+Uvicorn workers, or Container Apps. Both work.
caveats: If you need true autoscale-to-zero: prefer Container Apps.

spring-boot.recommended_path: Azure Spring Apps (managed Spring runtime) is the lowest-friction path. App Service Linux Java 17/21 and Container Apps also work.
caveats: Spring Apps Standard tier is paid but includes config server + service registry.
Container Apps is cheaper for simple deployments with no Spring-specific bindings.

dotnet.recommended_path: Azure App Service is the canonical .NET host. Functions for serverless. Container Apps for Docker. AAD identity is first-class via Microsoft.Identity.Web.
caveats: App Service .NET on Windows vs Linux: prefer Linux for new builds (cheaper, ARM64 supported).
Disable SCM basic auth via 'az webapp deployment policy update --name ... --type Allow=false'.

dotnet-blazor.recommended_path: Blazor WebAssembly → Static Web Apps (free tier covers it). Blazor Server → App Service Linux. Auto mode → App Service since you need a server runtime.
caveats: Blazor Server uses SignalR (WebSockets) — enable WebSockets on App Service.
WASM bundle size matters; trim aggressively.

websocket-heavy.recommended_path: Azure SignalR Service (managed) is the standard answer for WebSocket-heavy workloads. App Service supports WebSockets natively but scaling = SignalR Service. Container Apps + sticky sessions also works.
caveats: SignalR Service free tier is fine for dev; production needs Standard.
Long-lived connections bill on connection-hours.

long-running-compute.recommended_path: Azure Container Apps Jobs, Azure Batch, or AKS. Container Apps Jobs is the simplest for cron-style or queue-triggered batch.
caveats: Functions have a 10-minute default execution limit (60 min on Premium). For longer jobs use Container Apps Jobs.

media-processing-heavy.recommended_path: Azure Container Apps with FFmpeg base image, orchestrated from Azure Functions (queue trigger from Service Bus or Storage Queue), output to Blob Storage.
caveats: Sharp / native deps work fine on Linux Container Apps.
Browser Rendering / headless Chrome: use Container Apps with playwright base image.

mysql-app.recommended_path: Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server. Direct migration via mysqldump + restore. Use connection-string in Key Vault, App Service references it via 'azure-keyvault://' syntax.
caveats: Burstable tier saves money for dev/test but watches CPU credits.
Geo-redundant backup is paid + region-pair specific.
private endpoint = no public IP exposure.

postgres-app.recommended_path: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. Native Entra (AAD) auth. Connection pooling via PgBouncer is built-in on Flexible Server.
caveats: Read replicas are async; cross-region replicas are paid.
private endpoint + VNet integration removes public exposure.

mongodb-app.recommended_path: Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB API (vCore or RU-based). Native MongoDB-protocol-compatible. For exact-Mongo behavior, MongoDB Atlas on Azure marketplace is the safer answer.
caveats: Cosmos for MongoDB has compatibility matrix vs Atlas — check your specific aggregations.
RU-based pricing surprises new users; vCore is more familiar.

redis-app.recommended_path: Azure Cache for Redis. Three tiers: Basic / Standard / Premium. Premium adds clustering + persistence + VNet integration.
caveats: Basic tier has no SLA — dev/test only.
Premium is $$ — verify you actually need clustering before paying.

s3-storage.recommended_path: Azure Blob Storage. Migration: azcopy sync or AWS DataSync (S3 → Blob). For S3-API compatibility, use Azure's S3-compatible endpoint (preview) or keep app code with @azure/storage-blob.
caveats: Lifecycle policies map to Blob lifecycle management.
Public bucket access is OFF by default — control via container public access level.
S3 Select equivalent: Blob Query (preview) or pull-and-process.
dependencies_to_flag: @aws-sdk/client-s3 (works against S3-compatible Blob with endpoint override)
